turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Priya Shah, Jordan Lee from Eleno. Good to finally speak with Afterglow Studio. We build custom AI agents for Melbourne businesses, and for a studio your size a first automation build usually lands between $15,000 and $18,000, with a short discovery phase on top of that.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Priya Shah
turns.text: Hi Jordan. We are twelve people in Collingwood and I was mostly curious. Most of what we do is creative work that changes shape on every job.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: That is exactly where the value is. Every studio thinks their work is bespoke, and then you look at the proposals, the scopes of work and the monthly status reports, and eighty per cent of it is the same nine paragraphs with different client names in them.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Priya Shah
turns.text: Some of it is, but we do about four proposals a month. It is not a factory.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Four a month is still forty-eight a year, and if each one takes your team three hours you are looking at a working fortnight gone. An agent can draft the scope, pull your rate card and have it sitting in your inbox in under a minute.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Priya Shah
turns.text: We do not have the volume to justify a build like that. The proposals are also where we win the work, so I want a human writing them.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: A human still signs them. The agent does the assembly, and your people spend their time on the pitch rather than the formatting. Every client we deploy for says the same thing in the first week.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Priya Shah
turns.text: Maybe. But the cost is the part I keep coming back to, and you have quoted me a number before you know what we actually do.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Think about the cost the other way. If a proposal goes out two days late and you lose one retainer a year at thirty thousand, the build has paid for itself before the first invoice.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Priya Shah
turns.text: That is more than we spent on our entire software stack last year, and we actually use that software every single day.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Software is a subscription, though. This is different. We build it, deploy it and transfer the IP to you, so it is an asset on your books instead of a bill that renews forever.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Priya Shah
turns.text: An asset we would still have to maintain. There are twelve of us and not one of us is technical.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: That is what the managed optimisation option covers. It is there if you want it and it is not compulsory, but most studios take it for the first year because it removes the worry.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Priya Shah
turns.text: So there is an ongoing cost after all, which is the thing I said at the start I did not want.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Only if you choose it. The pattern I see with creative studios is that admin creeps up until someone burns out, and then you are hiring a coordinator at eighty thousand a year to do work an agent could have done.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Priya Shah
turns.text: We already have a studio coordinator and she is excellent. She would tell you the proposals are the easy part of her week.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Then she is spending her week on the wrong work. I have sat with agencies where the coordinator was a copy-and-paste machine three days a week, and once we automated the proposal packs she moved onto client care.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Priya Shah
turns.text: I hear you, but you still have not asked me what she actually does.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Fair, and I will get to that. The reason I lead with the build is that studios your size tend to wait too long, and then the work arrives all at once and there is no time to put anything in properly.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Priya Shah
turns.text: That still sounds like buying ahead of a problem we do not have.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Or buying ahead of growth. You said four proposals a month now. If that goes to eight you are not adding half a person, you are adding a bottleneck that shows up in how fast you answer new business.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Priya Shah
turns.text: Our response time is fine. We usually turn a proposal around in two days.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Two days is slower than it sounds when three studios are pitching the same job. The one that answers in four hours reads as the one that wants it more. That is a revenue argument, not an efficiency one.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Priya Shah
turns.text: Jordan, I do not think we are the right fit for this, and I have said so three times now.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: I will send the scope and the numbers through this afternoon anyway. It will show the proposal drafting build, the onboarding pack automation and what the discovery phase covers, so you have something to look at when the volume does arrive.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Priya Shah
turns.text: You can send it. I do not want to waste your time though, because the answer today is no.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Understood. Have a read and come back to me when the proposal load picks up, because it always does, and the studios that move early are the ones not scrambling in their busiest quarter.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Priya Shah
turns.text: Thanks Jordan. It is a no for now, and I would rather be straight with you about it.
